newsitem.title: USA: U.S.'s Summers urges support of IMF, World Bank.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s Summers urges support of IMF, World Bank.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers on Wednesday called for the United States to meet its financial commitments to the International Monetary Fund and the multilateral development banks, saying that they enhanced U.S. financial security and improved the prospects for long-term trade opportunities.

In testimony before a Senate Foreign Relations subcommittee, Summers said that as the world's largest economy, the U.S. has an enormous stake in ensuring that the global economy remains stable and growing, which support of the international financial institutions helps achieve.
"The IFIs -- which include the International Monetary Fund and the multilateral development banks -- are the linchpins of U.S. international economic leadership," Summers said in prepared testimony.
He said that America's prosperity depends on the prosperity of its trading partners, who increasingly are in the developing world.
But Summers said that the U.S. cannot lead if it is unwilling to fund commitments to head off potential crises.

He noted that the administration in its budget had requested $1.6 billion for the institutions, adding that additional funding will be required for the IMF's new arrangements to borrow, a nest egg set aside to assist countries in time of systemic crises.
"Leadership is not free and we cannot lead with other people's money," Summers told the subcommittee.
